items.title: The Promise and Limits of Predictive Flood Maps
items.topic: using computer models to decide where a rapidly growing city should restrict new construction
items.place: a river city expanding into low-lying land
items.action: compared historical floods, rainfall projections, model assumptions, and property data
items.benefit: risk maps could guide building rules and direct protective investment before disasters occur
items.challenge: models carried uncertainty, climate patterns were changing, and strict boundaries could reduce property values for some owners
items.lesson: decisions under uncertainty should make assumptions visible and remain adjustable as evidence changes
items.detail: officials proposed risk zones with scheduled reviews rather than treating one map as permanent truth
items.reflection: Aisha learned that uncertainty is not a reason to ignore evidence but a reason to design policies that can be revised
items.titleJa: 洪水予測地図の可能性と限界
items.topicJa: 成長都市で建設制限を決めるための洪水モデル利用
items.benefitJa: 災害前に建築規制や防災投資を導けること
items.challengeJa: モデルの不確実性・気候変化・資産価値への影響があること
items.lessonJa: 不確実な状況では前提を公開し新しい証拠に応じて修正できる政策が必要

items.title: Can an Algorithm Allocate Public Housing?
items.topic: a city testing an algorithm to prioritize applicants for limited public housing
items.action: examined the variables used by the ranking system and compared outcomes across applicant groups
items.benefit: consistent rules could process large numbers of applications faster and reduce some arbitrary decisions
items.challenge: past administrative data reflected unequal access to services, so apparently neutral variables could reproduce earlier disadvantages
items.lesson: automating a decision does not remove value judgments because choices about data, goals, and exceptions remain human choices
items.detail: the city required human review for unusual cases and published a simplified explanation of the scoring factors
items.reflection: Mateo learned that transparency must include not only how a system calculates but why those particular criteria were chosen
items.titleJa: アルゴリズムは公営住宅を配分できるか
items.topicJa: 限られた公営住宅の優先順位を決めるアルゴリズム
items.benefitJa: 多数の申請を一貫した基準で速く処理できる可能性
items.challengeJa: 過去データの格差を中立に見える変数が再現する可能性
items.lessonJa: 自動化してもデータ・目的・例外を選ぶ価値判断は人間に残る

items.title: A Forest Managed for More Than Timber
items.topic: balancing timber production, biodiversity, wildfire risk, and Indigenous cultural practices in a public forest
items.action: compared management plans using ecological surveys, employment data, fire history, and community knowledge
items.benefit: mixed management could support local jobs while protecting habitats and reducing dangerous fuel in selected areas
items.challenge: the goals operated on different time scales and evidence about some interventions remained uncertain
items.lesson: complex environmental management requires explicit trade-offs rather than pretending every objective can be maximized at once
items.detail: the final proposal used different zones, long-term monitoring, and periodic revision with community participation
items.reflection: Claire learned that a strong plan can be one that reveals conflicts clearly and creates a process for responding to new information
items.titleJa: 木材だけのためではない森林管理
items.topicJa: 木材生産・生物多様性・山火事・先住文化を両立させる森林管理
items.benefitJa: 雇用を支えつつ生息地保全や火災リスク低減を図れる可能性
items.challengeJa: 目標ごとに時間軸が異なり介入効果にも不確実性があること
items.lessonJa: 複雑な環境管理では全目標を最大化できるふりをせず取捨選択を明確にする必要がある

items.title: When Scientific Advice Changes
items.topic: how public agencies should communicate health guidance when new evidence changes earlier recommendations
items.place: a national public health communication team
items.action: studied how uncertainty, preliminary findings, and revised conclusions were explained to the public
items.benefit: timely guidance could help people act before every scientific question was settled
items.challenge: frequent changes could look like incompetence when audiences expected science to provide permanent answers
items.lesson: trust can depend less on never changing advice than on explaining what changed, why it changed, and how confident the evidence is
items.detail: the team began labeling recommendations by evidence strength and publishing short revision notes
items.reflection: Jun learned that correcting a recommendation can demonstrate a functioning evidence process rather than a failure of science
items.titleJa: 科学的助言が変わる時
items.topicJa: 新しい証拠で公衆衛生上の推奨が変わる場合の伝え方
items.benefitJa: 科学的疑問がすべて解決する前でも必要な行動を促せること
items.challengeJa: 助言変更が科学の無能さと受け取られる可能性
items.lessonJa: 信頼には助言を変えないことより何がなぜ変わり確信度がどの程度か説明することが重要
